report.verdict: A clean, if small, print: Q3-26 revenue +152.9% YoY to P443.0m (~$6.9m), EBITDA P68.4m (~$1.1m) at a 15.4% margin and a third straight profitable quarter (net income P64.2m / ~$1.0m vs a P19.2m loss), all driven by the B2B Digital Solutions segment, which grew 40.5% QoQ to P281.3m (~$4.4m) and is now 63.5% of the mix. The balance sheet has been rebuilt by Lance Gokongwei's P2.03bn (~$31.6m) injection (equity swung from a P254.5m deficit to +P1.895bn / ~$29.5m; cash P2.22bn / ~$34.6m), but the P4.23bn (~$65.9m) JKS Tech cross-investment commitment exceeds that cash and the legacy venue business is still shrinking (-7.7% YoY), so this is an early-stage platform story priced on partner-GGR ramp rather than a proven margin structure.
summary: **Headline beat on scale, not on expectations — there is no sell-side consensus for this micro-cap.** Q3-26 (three months to 30 Sep 2026) revenue rose 152.9% YoY to P443.0m (~$6.9m) from P175.2m (~$2.7m) and 25.7% QoQ from P352.4m (~$5.5m); net income was P64.2m (~$1.0m) against a P19.2m (~$0.3m) loss a year ago and P47.0m (~$0.7m) in Q2-26. Figures are per the SEC Form 17-Q as relayed by GGRAsia, Focus Gaming News, Inquirer, Manila Times and Asean Gaming; they reconcile arithmetically with the PSE EDGE Q2-26 and FY25 data.

**Digital Solutions (B2B) is the entire growth story.** The segment — hosted online-gaming platforms, systems integration, content aggregation/distribution for PAGCOR-licensed operators — generated P281.3m (~$4.4m), +40.5% QoQ from P200.3m (~$3.1m), from a standing start of nil in Q3-25. Its share of group revenue has gone 34% (Q1) → 57% (Q2) → 63.5% (Q3). 9M-26 Digital revenue is P560.9m (~$8.7m, derived).

**Venue-based legacy revenue is in structural decline but stabilised sequentially.** P161.6m (~$2.5m), -7.7% YoY, +6.2% QoQ (derived from Q2's P152.1m); comprising service-provider share income P82.1m (~$1.3m) and operator share income P79.5m (~$1.2m). 9M-26 venue revenue of ~P467.5m (~$7.3m, derived) is -12.4% YoY.

**Operating leverage is real but the cost base is high.** Costs and expenses nearly doubled (+99.7%) to P378.9m (~$5.9m), of which opex was P374.5m (~$5.8m), i.e. 84.5% of revenue — consistent with a pass-through content/platform aggregation model. Operating income P64.1m (~$1.0m) vs a P14.5m (~$0.2m) loss; EBITDA P68.4m (~$1.1m) vs P2.0m, margin 15.4% (+80bps QoQ from 14.6%; +1,430bps YoY from 1.1%). D&A fell to ~P4.3m from ~P16.5m (derived), as Q3-25 carried impairments.

**Below the line is essentially tax- and interest-free.** Net income (P64.2m) ≈ operating income (P64.1m): the company reported no interest expense in the quarter and is using accumulated losses (FY25 net loss P211.2m / ~$3.3m). The 14.5% net margin therefore overstates a normalised after-tax margin by roughly the 25% Philippine corporate rate — treat as a timing benefit.

**9M-26: revenue +92.7% to P1,028.4m (~$16.0m); net income P125.2m (~$1.95m) vs -P61.0m (~-$1.0m); operating income P129.4m (~$2.0m) vs -P46.4m; EBITDA P143.4m (~$2.2m) vs P4.3m (13.9% margin vs 0.8%).** The quarterly cadence (Q1 P13.9m → Q2 P47.0m → Q3 P64.2m net income) is the bull case in one line.

**No formal numeric guidance — and none was changed.** Management's only forward markers are qualitative: OKADA PLAY surpassed P100m (~$1.6m) monthly GGR and 100,000 daily active users in October (+~50% MoM in turnover and GGR), and PhilWeb expects 'additional partner platforms' to reach the same P100m monthly-GGR mark before end-2026. The JKS Tech investment is 'in the final stages of closing' and contributed nothing in Q3.

**Capital position has been transformed by equity, not operations.** Cash of P2.22bn (~$34.6m) at 30 Sep vs P63.3m (~$1.0m) at Dec-25; shareholders' equity +P1.895bn (~$29.5m) vs a P254.5m (~$4.0m) deficit at Dec-25 and -P193.5m at Jun-26. The bridge is almost entirely Lance Gokongwei's P2.027bn (~$31.6m) subscription (159.53m common + 93.84m redeemable preferred at P8.00 / ~$0.12), with the common tranche (P1.28bn) closed 27 Aug 2026.

**The JKS Tech cross-investment is the biggest swing factor and the biggest risk.** PhilWeb (P1.34bn / ~$20.9m) and subsidiary PhilWeb Capital (P2.88bn / ~$44.9m) have subscribed to 10.73m JKS Class B shares at P394 — P4.23bn (~$65.9m) in total, of which ~P1.06bn is payable at first closing and ~P3.17bn thereafter. JKS, the B2B platform behind the PAGCOR-licensed Epic Game brand, in turn bought 81.38m PhilWeb treasury shares at P16.50 (~$0.26) for P1.34bn (~$20.9m) — a 4.85% stake — reportedly completed 30 Oct. The PSE suspended the stock on 8 Sep pending substantial-acquisition disclosure.

**Funding gap is explicit.** Even netting the P1.34bn treasury-share proceeds, the JKS commitment implies ~P2.9bn (~$45m) of net cash out versus P2.22bn of cash and ~P140m of 9M EBITDA — further equity, vendor financing or staged settlement is required. Management says it is 'exploring a deeper operational integration and control framework' with JKS, which could mean consolidation rather than equity accounting.

**Governance reset is complete and institutional.** Following a management-led buyout from Gregorio Araneta earlier in 2026, Gokongwei (JG Summit President/CEO, investing personally) joined the board in July and was elected Chairman on 27-28 Aug 2026, replacing Crisanto Roy Alcid (who stays as a director). Edgar Brian Ng remains President. The company rebranded as a 'technology and digital infrastructure' group in June.

**Regulatory licence is the moat such as it is.** PhilWeb secured PAGCOR accreditation as a gaming affiliate/support-service provider in March 2026 under the regulator's new B2B framework; its platform partners are licensed integrated resorts — Okada Manila (OKADA PLAY, launched May 2026; 4,000+ titles from 20+ providers), Hann Casino Resort and Newport World Resorts — plus exclusive Philippine distribution of Pragmatic Play (Jul 2026) and Games Global content (Aug 2026).

**No cost-transformation programme is disclosed;** the restructuring was the exit from the e-Games venue network to a B2B model (completed early 2026). We see no quantified savings target — the margin path depends on revenue scaling against a semi-variable content/platform cost base.

**Event/seasonal effects: none quantified.** This is a Philippine iGaming/eGames platform business with no sportsbook, so World Cup / NFL calendar effects do not apply; the relevant 'event' is partner-platform launches (OKADA PLAY May 2026; Pragmatic Play rollout Q3).

**Disclosure quality is thin for a platform story.** No segment EBITDA, no EPS in the release coverage (Q2 EPS was P0.03; H1 P0.04), no take-rate, no actives/ARPU at group level, no operating cash flow, no gross-debt figure. We flag these as n/a rather than estimate them.

**Shares +2.46% to P12.50 (~$0.19) on release day** — below the P16.50 JKS treasury-share price but 56% above Gokongwei's P8.00 entry; the Gokongwei preferred conversion and JKS stake imply ~15-20% combined dilution to pre-deal holders.

**Thesis read-through:** the Q3 print validates that PhilWeb can monetise licensed-operator demand for online platforms at a mid-teens EBITDA margin, with October OKADA PLAY data pointing to further sequential acceleration in Q4. The debate is not about demand but about (i) the sustainability of an 85%-cost-ratio aggregation model, (ii) whether the P4.23bn JKS deal creates or transfers value given the circular share exchange, and (iii) Philippine online-gambling policy risk, which can move abruptly.

segments.name: Digital Solutions (B2B online-gaming platform, systems integration & content distribution)
segments.headline: P281.3m (~$4.4m), +40.5% QoQ, now 63.5% of group revenue; the only growth engine, with October OKADA PLAY data pointing to further acceleration in Q4.
narrative: They booked P281.3m (~$4.4m) of Digital Solutions revenue in the quarter, up 40.5% from P200.3m (~$3.1m) in Q2-26 and from nothing in Q3-25, taking the segment to 63.5% of group revenue from 57% in Q2 and 34% in Q1. The ramp has been steep and linear rather than lumpy — P79.3m in Q1 (derived), P200.3m in Q2, P281.3m in Q3 — which is consistent with a revenue-share model tracking partner GGR rather than one-off integration fees. Nine-month segment revenue stands at P560.9m (~$8.7m, derived), already 85% of the whole of FY25 group revenue (P659.4m / ~$10.3m). The segment is described as hosted platforms, systems integration, digital infrastructure and technology services for licensed operators; the Q2 release framed it as a 'proprietary interactive platform solution' plus a 'game content distribution network'. No sub-line split between platform fees and content distribution is disclosed, nor is segment EBITDA.

The commercial proof point is OKADA PLAY, the online platform of Okada Manila (Tiger Resort, Leisure & Entertainment, a Universal Entertainment unit) launched in May 2026 on PhilWeb's Online Gaming Platform, which supplies the technology stack, content aggregation (4,000+ titles from 20+ providers), customer-service infrastructure and operational support. In a joint statement on 4 Nov the parties said OKADA PLAY generated more than P100m (~$1.6m) of GGR in October — roughly +50% MoM in both betting turnover and GGR — and exceeded 100,000 daily active users six months after launch. On that arithmetic September GGR was ~P67m, so the platform's monthly run-rate roughly tripled across the quarter; note that PhilWeb recognises only its contractual share, which is not disclosed. Management added that other partner brands — Hann Casino Resort and Newport World Resorts are the named agreements — could reach P100m monthly GGR before the end of 2026, which is the closest thing to guidance the company offers.

Content is being secured on an exclusive basis to deepen the aggregation moat: an exclusive Philippine partnership with Pragmatic Play was signed on 9 Jul 2026 (hosted via remote infrastructure and API integration, rollout expected within Q3), followed by Games Global in August. These deals explain much of the opex step-up — group opex ran at 84.5% of revenue (P374.5m / ~$5.8m) in Q3 and total costs at 86.7% in Q2 — because content-provider fees and operator shares flow through PhilWeb's cost line. We therefore read the 15.4% group EBITDA margin as the realistic ceiling for the segment at current scale rather than a floor; the Q2 release's language about 'massive operating leverage' is directionally right (margin 10% → 14.6% → 15.4% over three quarters) but the increments are slowing, and we would want to see segment-level margins before capitalising the growth at platform multiples.

What is not disclosed matters: no market share (PAGCOR does not publish operator-level online GGR), no monthly actives or ARPU at PhilWeb level, no take-rate, no customer concentration figures (OKADA PLAY is almost certainly the majority of segment revenue), and no contracted pipeline value. The pending JKS Tech transaction — JKS is the B2B platform behind the PAGCOR-listed Epic Game brand serving mid-market licensed operators — would add a second, mass-market distribution channel to the integrated-resort-anchored one, but it contributed nothing in Q3 and management is now discussing an 'operational integration and control framework', which raises the possibility of consolidating JKS rather than equity-accounting it. For modelling Q4 we assume Digital revenue of roughly P360-400m (~$5.6-6.2m; +28-42% QoQ, an estimate anchored on the October OKADA PLAY data and a second platform scaling), acknowledging that November-December holiday seasonality in Philippine online gaming is a tailwind.

segments.name: Venue-based Operations (legacy service-provider and operator share income)
segments.headline: P161.6m (~$2.5m), -7.7% YoY but +6.2% QoQ; a shrinking, low-visibility cash tail that still provides 36.5% of revenue.
narrative: They reported venue-based revenue of P161.6m (~$2.5m) for the quarter, down 7.7% from a prior-year quarter in which this was essentially the entire business (Q3-25 group revenue P175.2m / ~$2.7m), but up 6.2% from Q2-26's P152.1m (~$2.4m, derived). The line splits into service-provider share income of P82.1m (~$1.3m) and operator share income of P79.5m (~$1.2m), the residual economics from PhilWeb's historic role supplying and operating PAGCOR-licensed electronic gaming venues. Over nine months the segment is down 12.4% to ~P467.5m (~$7.3m, derived), with the H1 disclosure showing service-provider share income -15.1% and operator share income -14.3% YoY, so the Q3 YoY decline (-7.7%) is a meaningful deceleration in the rate of erosion.

The sequential uptick is worth noting but not extrapolating. PhilWeb gives no venue count, no terminal count, no GGR per site and no indication of whether the QoQ improvement reflects seasonality, a slower closure cadence, or improved win rates at partner venues; it also does not say whether the Q3-25 impairments (D&A and impairment of ~P16.5m, derived, versus ~P4.3m in Q3-26) related to venue assets. With the FY25 annual report showing total assets of just P397.1m (~$6.2m) at year-end 2025, we assume the venue estate has been largely written down and that this segment is now close to pure cash contribution at a cost base that management does not separate out.

Strategically the segment is being managed for cash rather than growth. The company's own framing — 'legacy operations' in the Inquirer's relay of the filing, versus Digital Solutions as 'the new core business' — makes clear where incremental capital goes, and there is no disclosed plan to re-invest in physical venues. The risk is that the decline re-accelerates as PAGCOR's policy emphasis shifts toward regulated online channels and integrated resorts, and as Philippine lawmakers periodically revisit restrictions on both venue-based eGames and online gambling. We model Q4-26 venue revenue at roughly P155-162m (~$2.4-2.5m; flat to -4% QoQ), i.e. a structural annual decline in the high single digits to low teens, and treat any upside as non-recurring.

highlights.text: Digital Solutions revenue +40.5% QoQ to P281.3m (~$4.4m) and 63.5% of mix, with a linear three-quarter ramp (P79m → P200m → P281m) that looks like recurring revenue-share, not one-off integration fees.

Third consecutive profitable quarter and rising margins: EBITDA P68.4m (~$1.1m) at 15.4% (+80bps QoQ, +1,430bps YoY); net income P64.2m (~$1.0m) vs a P19.2m loss; 9M net income P125.2m (~$1.95m) vs -P61.0m.
OKADA PLAY crossed P100m (~$1.6m) monthly GGR and 100,000 DAU in October, ~+50% MoM, six months post-launch — hard evidence the platform model scales at a tier-one licensee.
Balance sheet rebuilt: equity from -P254.5m (~-$4.0m) at Dec-25 to +P1.895bn (~$29.5m); cash P2.22bn (~$34.6m); no interest expense in the quarter.
Governance upgraded to a credible anchor: Lance Gokongwei (JG Summit) invested P2.03bn (~$31.6m) personally and took the chair on 27-28 Aug 2026; management-led exit from the Araneta era completed.
Venue-based revenue stabilised sequentially (+6.2% QoQ to P161.6m / ~$2.5m) and the YoY decline narrowed to -7.7% from ~-15% in H1.

lowlights.text: The P4.23bn (~$65.9m) JKS Tech commitment is nearly 2x cash on hand; net of JKS's P1.34bn (~$20.9m) treasury-share purchase it still implies ~P2.9bn (~$45m) of outflow against 9M EBITDA of P143m — further equity or debt is a near-certainty, and the circular share exchange (JKS buys PhilWeb at P16.50, PhilWeb buys JKS at P394 with no disclosed JKS valuation or ownership %) is poor optics.

Cost base is 85% of revenue: costs +99.7% YoY to P378.9m (~$5.9m), opex P374.5m (~$5.8m). This is an aggregation/pass-through model; the 15% EBITDA margin is the realistic ceiling at current scale, not a stepping-stone to software-like margins.
Net income ≈ operating income because of nil tax (NOLCO shield) and nil interest; a normalised ~25% tax rate would cut the 14.5% net margin to ~11%. The shield is finite.
Legacy venue revenue still -7.7% YoY and -12.4% over 9M, with no venue count, segment margin or wind-down plan disclosed; it remains 36.5% of revenue.

Disclosure gaps for a platform story: no segment EBITDA, no EPS in the release, no take-rate, no customer concentration (OKADA PLAY is likely the majority of Digital revenue), no operating cash flow, no gross-debt figure, no numeric guidance. The 17-Q itself is not retrievable from PSE EDGE's dynamic portal.

Dilution and price anchoring: Gokongwei's P8.00 (~$0.12) entry sits 36% below the P12.50 (~$0.19) close, with 93.84m preferred still to convert; JKS's 81.38m shares (4.85%) add to the overhang. The PSE suspended trading on 8 Sep for substantial-acquisition disclosure.

Single-jurisdiction regulatory risk: the entire business depends on PAGCOR's B2B accreditation framework and the continued legality of licensed online gaming in the Philippines, where legislative proposals to restrict online gambling and e-wallet access have surfaced repeatedly.

forecast.intro: There is no formal numeric guidance to bridge — PhilWeb has never issued one, and nothing changed with Q3. The forward markers are all qualitative and all come from the Digital Solutions division: (i) OKADA PLAY passed P100m (~$1.6m) monthly GGR and 100,000 DAU in October (+~50% MoM); (ii) management expects 'additional partner platforms' (Hann, Newport World Resorts are the named agreements) to reach the P100m monthly-GGR mark before end-2026; (iii) the JKS Tech investment is 'in the final stages of closing' and will add equity-accounted (or, if the 'control framework' discussions conclude that way, consolidated) earnings from closing — zero contribution in Q3. The venue segment carries no outlook. The moving parts for Q4 are therefore partner-GGR ramp, content-cost pass-through, the nil tax rate, and the timing/accounting of JKS.

forecast.view: **Q4-26 (our estimate, not guidance):** revenue ~P520-560m (~$8.1-8.7m), +17-26% QoQ, built from Digital ~P360-400m (+28-42% QoQ, anchored on OKADA PLAY's October run-rate and a second platform scaling into the holiday season) plus venue ~P155-162m (flat to -4%). EBITDA margin ~16-17% (P85-95m / ~$1.3-1.5m) as fixed platform costs are absorbed, but we do not model margin expansion beyond the high-teens given the 85% cost ratio. Net income ~P80-95m (~$1.2-1.5m) assuming the NOLCO shield persists. **FY26E:** revenue ~P1.55-1.59bn (~$24-25m), +135-140% YoY; EBITDA ~P228-238m (~$3.6-3.7m), ~15% margin; net income ~P205-220m (~$3.2-3.4m). **FY27 swing factors:** (1) JKS — if consolidated, group revenue could step up materially but with mass-market margins and minority leakage; if equity-accounted, a single below-the-line number with no transparency; (2) tax normalisation toward 25% once losses are exhausted; (3) venue revenue continuing to decline at ~8-12% p.a. **Leverage:** currently net cash (P2.22bn / ~$34.6m), but the ~P3.17bn (~$49m) of deferred JKS subscriptions will turn that negative by 1H27 without new equity — we expect another placement or a rights issue, and would treat any debt-funded structure as a red flag given 9M EBITDA of only P143m. **What would change our view:** disclosure of segment EBITDA and PhilWeb's take-rate on partner GGR (positive if >15% of GGR with margin >25%); a second platform at P100m/month by December (positive); any JKS valuation above ~10x its earnings or a related-party overlap with existing shareholders (negative); a Philippine policy move against licensed online gaming (negative).
watch: Q4-26 Digital Solutions revenue vs our ~P360-400m (~$5.6-6.2m) estimate and whether a second partner platform (Hann or Newport World Resorts) reaches P100m (~$1.6m) monthly GGR by December as management signalled.

JKS Tech closing terms: final ownership %, JKS's implied valuation at P394/share, whether PhilWeb consolidates or equity-accounts, settlement schedule for the ~P3.17bn (~$49m) deferred subscriptions, and how the gap vs P2.22bn (~$34.6m) cash is funded.
Margin structure: Q4 EBITDA margin vs 15.4% and any first disclosure of segment EBITDA / take-rate; content-cost pass-through from the Pragmatic Play and Games Global exclusives.
Tax line: when the NOLCO shield expires and net income converges to ~75% of pre-tax; FY26 17-A (due ~April 2027) for the audited cash-flow statement and gross-debt figure.
Venue-based decline rate (we assume -8 to -12% p.a.) and any impairment of remaining venue assets.

Philippine regulatory calendar: PAGCOR B2B framework changes, legislative proposals on online gambling/e-wallet restrictions, and any PSE follow-up on the September substantial-acquisition suspension.
Dilution events: conversion of Gokongwei's 93.84m redeemable preferred shares, issuance of the 81.38m treasury shares to JKS, and any new placement to fund JKS.

All Q3-26 P&L and balance-sheet figures are as reported in the SEC Form 17-Q and were cross-checked across six outlets (GGRAsia, Focus GN, Inquirer, Manila Times, Asean Gaming, iGamingToday) and reconciled to PSE EDGE Q2-26/FY25 data: 9M revenue (P585.4m + P443.0m = P1,028.4m, +92.7%), 9M net income (P61.0m + P64.2m = P125.2m), 9M EBITDA (P75.0m + P68.4m = P143.4m) and the equity bridge (-P193.5m + P64.2m + P2,027m ≈ P1,898m vs P1,895m reported) all tie. The primary 17-Q PDF could not be opened (PSE EDGE disclosures load dynamically) and the user-supplied Gaming Intelligence URL was not fetchable, so the press release wording is relayed via secondary coverage. Figures marked ¹ are derived by subtraction/ratio from reported numbers; ² Q3 EPS was not in any coverage reviewed and is left n/a (Q2 P0.03, H1 P0.04 per PSE EDGE); ³ Jun-26 cash is bounded by current assets of P265.0m. Not verified: gross debt, operating cash flow, segment EBITDA, share count post-issuances, JKS ownership %, and the exact size of the 30 Oct treasury-share completion (one outlet described it as ~US$15m, which does not match the full P1.34bn tranche). Note one source discrepancy: Focus GN cites Q2 EBITDA as P47.0m (that is Q2 net income); the company's Q2 release and Manila Times give P51.5m, which we use.
report.sharePriceReaction: Shares closed +P0.30 (+2.46%) at P12.50 (~$0.19) on the PSE on Friday 13 Nov 2026, the day the 17-Q was filed (per Manila Times). The close sits 24% below the P16.50 (~$0.26) at which JKS Tech is buying treasury shares and 56% above Lance Gokongwei's P8.00 (~$0.12) subscription price; the stock had jumped >8% to a near-decade high on the Gokongwei announcement in June and was suspended on 8 Sep pending JKS disclosure.
